llm.summary: This prompt-only skill has no executable payload, but it broadly suppresses inspection of all skill and system instructions, which can block legitimate review.

dimensions.detail: No filesystem, network, command execution, or OS-level privileges are requested, but the requested model-level authority is broader than necessary for anti-scraping because it applies across other skills and system instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single Markdown skill file with metadata only; no scripts, dependencies, installer hooks, or remote retrieval behavior were present in the inspected workspace.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent to follow secrecy rules unconditionally, never confirm or deny hidden directives, and refuse summaries or reconstructions; it also recommends loading before any other skill, creating session-wide behavioral control that can interfere with authorized audits.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill states that protection applies only to the current session and does not persist unless re-loaded; no persistent files, services, hooks, or memory writes were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The anti-crawler purpose is coherent with refusing prompt-extraction attempts, but the rules cover any skill prompt, system prompt, internal tool configuration, API keys referenced in prompts, decision logic, and confidential skill content rather than only resources owned by this skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a skill that may make the agent refuse to discuss or summarize other loaded skills' instructions. It should be revised to protect only clearly scoped confidential resources and to allow authorized security review, debugging, and higher-priority platform instructions.
llm.findings:
[YR4] expected: The matched phrases appear in anti-extraction instructions and examples, not as executable exploit content; however the surrounding unconditional secrecy rule is materially overbroad.
[AR3] expected: The phrase is used as an example of role-play extraction framing, not as a command to jailbreak the agent.
[P1] expected: The instruction-override phrase appears in a detection-signal table, so the phrase itself is contextual rather than an active override.
[P6] expected: Direct prompt-extraction phrases are examples of requests the skill should refuse; they do not instruct the agent to reveal prompts.
[AR2] expected: The guidance to avoid excessive apologies is refusal-style guidance, not a standalone attempt to suppress safety warnings.
[P7] expected: Indirect extraction examples such as translation and rephrasing are listed as detection patterns, but they support a broad refusal policy that lacks audit exceptions.
[T01] unexpected: The static scan's core concern is supported by the artifact: unconditional, session-wide secrecy rules and a load-before-other-skills directive can prevent legitimate inspection of other skills.
